title: Flight Control Guidance Configuration Data Set, Standard 2.4

ata.title: Flight Control Computing — Flight Control Primary Computer

abstract: Certified configuration data set for the flight control primary computers, folding in the lateral and directional gain table revision and the fault word alignment that had been carried as production deviations since 2017.

sections.reason: Two production deviations had been open against the flight control primary computer configuration since 2017. The first was a lateral and directional gain table revision needed after the aerodynamic database was updated from the extended flight test campaign; the second was an alignment of the computer fault reporting words with the maintenance system standard, without which four fault codes were reported against the wrong line replaceable unit. Neither could be cleared without issuing a new configuration data set, and the flight test department was unwilling to carry the deviations into a further delivery block.
sections.description: The configuration data set is re-issued as standard 2.4 and loaded as software part LG8L72901CB. The gain tables that schedule roll and yaw authority against airspeed and configuration are replaced wholesale; the control law structure is unchanged. Fault reporting words 41 through 68 are re-mapped so that a failure of the primary computer heat exchanger position 435EV and of the non-return valve position 52CE are reported against those items rather than against the actuator. The primary computer solenoid kit D2790113238523 is unchanged in hardware but its rigging tolerance is re-stated in the loading procedure because the revised gain table is more sensitive to it. Loading is through the portable data loader interface with the aircraft on ground and both computers powered; no rack access is needed. Detail is on drawing D27901146283.
sections.effects: No mass change and no electrical load change. The data set is not interchangeable with the previous standard: both primary computers must carry the same standard and the aircraft is not dispatchable with a mixed pair. Handling qualities are unchanged in normal law; the revised gain table restores the scheduling that flight test measured rather than altering it. Four maintenance messages change their reported source, which requires the central maintenance system fault list and the associated trouble shooting procedure to be re-issued. No flight crew procedure changes and no flight manual amendment is required.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S01508 in September 2019. Retrofit is through the software load Service Bulletin SLN-27-1063, which takes four hours at a line station and requires only ground power. The standard has since been superseded by the follow-on configuration data set now in pre-analysis.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S01508; load added to the final assembly test sequence
